{"prompt":"You are the brainstorming worker for a C -> Rust translation of a small TOTP (time-based one-time password) codebase.

Source files (in the workspace root): totp.c, totp.h, std.c, std.h, main.c, test.c, Makefile, README.md, LICENSE.md.

Target: Rust, built and tested with `cargo test`.

Your task (brainstorm only, NO code writing):
1. Read all the source files in the workspace.
2. List the core difficulties of translating this codebase to Rust (e.g., the sha1 function clobbers its input buffer and requires capacity checks; the NO_STD freestanding path; the __attribute__((visibility)) export macro; the base32 decoding with padding; the CLI and test harness differences).
3. Propose a candidate approach: crate layout (single crate, lib + bins), how to map each C file to Rust modules, how to handle the buffer-clobbering sha1 API (keep same signature with &mut [u8] + cap, or redesign), how to port the tests (assert-based test.c -> #[test] functions), and how to handle the CLI (main.c -> src/main.rs).
4. Write your findings to notes.md in the workspace root (append, don't overwrite existing content).

Work only inside your workspace. When done, report a summary of the difficulties and your recommended approach."}
